findings.text: LBR virtualization enablement is exposed as a per-vCPU helper that both activates the feature and refreshes related interception controls.
Bulk vCPU locking, bulk unlocking, and a creation-progress query are exposed for whole-VM operations that must stabilize every vCPU.

Bulk acquisition requires the VM lock to be held, refuses with busy status while creation is incomplete, takes vCPU mutexes in enumeration order with interruptible nested semantics, releases already acquired entries on interruption, while bulk release drops every vCPU mutex under the same VM lock.

Encrypted save-area update is restricted to enhanced guests, runs once per vCPU under the bulk lock, rejects vCPUs under guest debugging, validates the area before firmware handling, flushes its backing page ahead of in-place encryption, and only afterward marks floating state confidential and protected before turning on LBR virtualization.

Pre-encryption synchronization captures general instruction state plus selected extended control, protection-key, supervisor-state and debug state and feature flags, with non-default VM types additionally capturing legacy floating, vector and extended component state using split placement for legacy registers and zero fill when a component is absent.

Measurement, attestation, outbound session establishment and outbound data update share a two-phase userspace protocol where a zero length asks only for firmware-reported sizes and a nonzero length supplies bounded buffers whose results and firmware error are returned to the caller.

Launch completion, guest status query, outbound completion and outbound cancellation first verify a secure-guest context and forward the stored handle to firmware, with status additionally reporting back policy, lifecycle state and handle.

Debug crypt walks the requested span in slices bounded by remaining length and by source and destination page offsets, pins both pages, flushes them, uses a direct firmware operation when alignment requirements are met and otherwise uses a staged temporary-buffer operation, always unpinning each slice before continuing or returning.

The unaligned staging allocator normalizes the start downward to firmware granularity, expands the span to cover the full request including a possible split tail, keeps the translated access inside one page, uses an isolated whole page on hosts with active memory-integrity protection and a sized heap buffer otherwise, with a matching release operation.

Unaligned decrypt stages firmware output and then transfers only the requested bytes to userspace with offset correction, while unaligned encrypt first stages decrypted destination content, merges incoming userspace bytes at the right offset, then re-encrypts the staged span back to the destination.

Secret injection pins and flushes the guest range, requires the backing pages to be physically contiguous, stages separate transport and header inputs, performs firmware encryption into the guest location, then marks every involved page dirty and recently used before unpinning.

Outbound data update pins exactly one guest page, rejects empty pointers, zero lengths and spans crossing a page boundary, tags the guest address for encrypted access, stages header and transport areas, and copies both results back to userspace after firmware handling.

Secure-guest controls are gated by guest flavor, with enhanced-only paths rejecting other guests and general paths rejecting non-secure guests, debug direction selecting between decrypt and encrypt firmware operations, migration split into start, data, completion and cancellation phases, and inbound start validating peer and session material before creating an encryption context.

Stale cached plaintext, concurrent access under integrity protection, creation races, firmware granularity violations, cross-page accesses and userspace range wrap are guarded by explicit flushes, isolated staging pages, busy rejection, slow paths, page-span checks and overflow validation, alongside a one-time warning for unsupported debugging of enhanced guests.

Firmware exchange uses a kernel descriptor carrying handle, physical addresses and lengths, paired with a userspace envelope carrying pointers, lengths and operation-specific fields such as policy and session sizes, with firmware-computed lengths echoed back even for size queries.

Userspace firmware blobs have an upper bound, save-area encryption operates on one page, debug operations use sixteen-byte granularity, and failures are reported with distinct standard errors for wrong guest type, inaccessible userspace, invalid argument, allocation failure and concurrent creation.
